newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends lower, but back from nadir.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends lower, but back from nadir.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed lower on Monday against its U.S. counterpart on the greenback's strength overseas, but late buying by local banks pulled the local currency back from its intraday low, dealers said.
The local unit ended at T$27.573 against Thursday's T$27.559 close. Turnover was a heavy US$357.5 million.
The market was closed on Friday and Saturday for a holiday.
The Taiwan dollar had sunk as low as T$27.609 early in the session, mainly reflecting the American currency's recent strong showing against the Japanese yen, dealer said.
But the rate stabilised in afternoon trade with local banks selling off U.S. dollars, dealers said.
"The banks do not feel the U.S. dollar has much room to rise further, especially since the central bank has hinted it would not let the local currency fall too much," said one dealer.
A central bank vice governor said on Thursday the foreign exchange market should not have "false expectations" of a Taiwan dollar depreciation, a comment that halted a slide.
Dealers expected the Taiwan dollar to continue a gradual downtrend as the U.S. currency gains overseas. A T$27.55-60 range was seen for Tuesday. --Kevin Chen (5080815)
